proposal.summary: CM550 sets up its J1939 transmit side at start-up. Each descriptor set-up writes a j1939_transmit_message_t: the header (PGN << 8, with the priority word from e2m block 1254 & 7 << 2 in the top byte and j1939_engine_node_source_address in the low byte), the data length, the data pointer and the status pointer. Many set-ups also register a PGN 59904 request responder with registerJ1939PgnRequestHandler. Three of the listed set-ups match CM848 step for step (DM10, EEC2 and the extra DM8 set-up are twins). Two differ by one store (the DM1 and ACK set-ups). The PGN 65257 / 65244 / 65255 set-ups have no CM848 counterpart. Each sender builds one message: the PGN 59392 acknowledgement (control byte 0 = ACK / 1 = NACK; it echoes the request's first three data bytes and is addressed to the requester) and the DM8 test result sent from the DM7 handler. A PGN 61184 request arrives as a can_standard_receive_descriptor_t: the 18-byte CAN ring record, or the transport reassembly record 0x8012cc. cm550_dispatchJ1939DiagnosticServiceRequest finds data byte 0 in j1939_diagnostic_service_table, runs the length / key check, calls the handler and answers with the handler's result byte. The memory read / write handlers return their worker's result unchanged, so the workers need real return types (the read worker's existing 'void' row is wrong). The J1587 helpers size PID fields for the J1708 request parser. The RC builder's '=' bug writes 1 into the engine brake driver count.

functions.role: Sends a J1939 Acknowledgement (PGN 59392) for a received request: the control byte from its argument and the request's first three data bytes, addressed to the requester.

functions.plate_comment: Sends the J1939 Acknowledgement (PGN 59392, j1939_pgn59392_tx_message) for a received request. The header is 0xe8ff00 with the priority j1939_pgn59392_priority_cal (e2m 1254 +0 JCAKPZ) & 7, and it is addressed back to the requester: header byte 2 = the request's source address, byte 3 = the address the request went to. Payload byte 1 is the control byte acknowledgement_type (0 = ACK, 1 = NACK) and bytes 6-8 are the request's data bytes 1-3 (the requested PGN for a PGN 59904 request); bytes 2-5 keep the 0xff of cm550_initializePgn59392AcknowledgementBuffer. Callers: cm550_j1939HandlePgn65228Dm3ClearInactiveFaults (0 after a DM3), cm550_receivePgn58112Dm7CommandNonContinuouslyMonitoredTestMessage (1 for an unsupported test) and cm550_dispatchJ1939PgnRequest (1 when no responder matched a request that was not global). Counterpart of CM848 0x23dbc, which addresses the same payload to the global address 0xff (was cm550_diagnosticCanResponseSender; PR #53 round 97).

Its only caller is the J1708 request parser 0x1e956 (named buildPgn65228Dm3ClearInitMessage), right after it reads the PID byte: a 0 stops the parse, otherwise it is added to the bytes consumed. It takes no argument and returns a byte. CM848 has no J1587 link (was cm550_insiteParameterParser; PR #53 round 97).

functions.plate_comment: Returns how many bytes the ECM's reply for the requested J1587 PID (insite_parameter_id) will take, the PID byte included. Values: 2 below PID 128 and 3 below 192. PID 193: insite_active_fault_count + 2. PID 194: two bytes per code ((active_j1922_reportable_fault_count + insite_fault_change_queue_count) x 2 + 2), or three with insite_full_detail_response_mode ((active_j1922_reportable_fault_count + inactive_fault_j1587_reportable_count) x 3 + 2). It is the only caller of cm848_validateJ1939DiagnosticRequest. The new name is a verb phrase and matches the CM550 counterpart.
cm848_functions.plate_comment: The PGN 61184 receive handler, registered by registerJ1939DiagnosticServiceDispatcher and also fed by the transport reassembly. A received 0x0c / 0x0d (a response) gets no handler and no reply. Otherwise it looks data byte 0 up in j1939_diagnostic_service_table, runs cm848_validateJ1939DiagnosticRequest and, when that returns 0xff, the entry's handler, then answers with cm848_sendJ1939ResponseFrame unless the result is 0xff (0x18 when no entry matches). Counterpart of CM550's cm550_dispatchJ1939DiagnosticServiceRequest, which has no response-service filter (was cm848_j1939DiagnosticServiceHandler; PR #53 round 97).
cm848_functions.evidence: 0x22128-0x221ec: lwz 6(r29) / lbz the service; li r31,24; cmpwi 12 / 13 -> li r31,255 @0x22150-0x22160; scan of 0x3fa8b2 with the count 0x3fa972; bl 0x50b634 then blrl to the handler; bl 0x249c4 cm848_sendJ1939ResponseFrame unless 255. Medium only because many CM848 plates refer to the current name.

roles.role: Sends the J1939 Acknowledgment (PGN 59392) for a received frame. Header 0xe8ff00 with the priority (word 0x803f4e, e2m 1254 +0 JCAKPZ 'default priority for ACK message') & 7 << 2. The destination (ID byte 2) is the requester's source address (request ID byte 3), and the source (ID byte 3) is the address the request was sent to (request ID byte 2). Data byte 1 (0x801eb2) is the control byte argument. Data bytes 6-8 (0x801eb7-9) are request->data_pointer[0..2]. It ends with cm550_sendCanMessage(j1939_pgn59392_tx_message 0x801ea4). Bytes 2-5 = 0xff and length 8 come from 0x31b96.

It answers the requester directly, not the global address. Prototype (already in place): void (can_standard_receive_descriptor_t *request +4, word acknowledgement_type +8).

roles.role: Builds and sends DM1 (PGN 65226) while j1939_dm1_transmit_status has no 0xf0 bit. With no active fault it sends lamp byte 0 and 0xffffffff (length 6). Otherwise it sends the lamp byte from cm550_buildJ1939LampStatusByte, then for each active_dtc_list slot whose fault definition word lacks 0x4000, a 4-byte DTC. The DTC is built from the table word at ROM 0x60fac (top 19 bits), the FMI (0x60fae & 0x1f) << 8, the occurrence count capped at 127 and 0x80. The output pointer advances for skipped slots too (addq.l #4,a2 at 0x323a0), so a skipped slot leaves a 4-byte gap, and the length counts only the written DTCs.

roles.role: Returns the byte count (PID included) of the J1587 parameter being parsed in a received J1708 message. It reads PID = insite_parameter_id (0x80dde5): PID 0-127 -> 2, 128-191 -> 3, 192-253 -> the length byte at insite_request_read_pointer (0x80ddf2, the byte after the PID) + 2, or 20 when that byte is above 18, 254-255 -> 0 (asm 0x2ed6a-0x2edb0).

roles.cm848_counterpart: none: CM848 has no J1708 / J1587 parameter handling

roles.role: The PGN 61184 request handler and service dispatcher. The request is the long at +4. The result starts at 0x18 (unknown service). On a match the result is cm550_diagnosticServiceSecurityValidator(request), and when that is 0xff the result is the handler's (move.l a3,-(a7); jsr (a0); low byte of d0). A result other than 0xff goes to cm550_diagnosticMultiPacketResponseBuilder(request, result) (asm 0x2eea2-0x2ef06).
